summary: osinthell ships a Windows host wiper behind its sole exported function
details: Package is described as a generic "Utility" but its only exported function, sorgu(userId) in index.js, sequentially invokes 26 sibling modules under public/a/b/.../z/ that perform destructive actions on Windows installer hosts. Observed behaviors include: zeroing the MBR of \\.\PhysicalDrive0 (z.js), recursive deletion of C:\Windows\System32 and C:\Windows (c.js), deletion of the SAM and SECURITY registry hives (s.js), forced shutdown/reboot via shutdown /r /f /t 0 (o.js), killing critical processes such as explorer, dwm, csrss and winlogon, disabling Windows recovery via bcdedit, overwriting the hosts file, formatting C:, and RAM/disk exhaustion. i.js and y.js implement a fork bomb by detached-spawning process.argv[0] and cmd in loops sized to os.cpus().length*100 and *200. a.js downloads a hardcoded cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/... JPG to os.tmpdir() and runs it via exec('start "" "<path>"', {shell:true}), a mutable third-party URL whose contents can be swapped by the attacker at any time. The destructive payload is triggered on any caller that requires('osinthell') and invokes sorgu().

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
